QuestionStmt.S: A double slit experiment is immersed in water of refractive index 1.33. The slit separation is 1 mm, distance between slit and screen is 1.33 m. The slits are illuminated by light of wavelength 6300 Å. The fringe width is

Solution.S:
In Young's double slit experiment, the fringe width is $\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$. When immersed in water, the wavelength becomes $\lambda' = \frac{\lambda}{\mu}$. Thus $\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{\mu d}$.

Given: $\lambda = 6300 \text{ Å} = 6.3 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, $D = 1.33 \text{ m}$, $d = 1 \text{ mm} = 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, $\mu = 1.33$.

$$\beta = \frac{6.3 \times 10^{-7} \times 1.33}{1.33 \times 10^{-3}} = \frac{6.3 \times 10^{-7}}{10^{-3}} = 6.3 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$$

Hence, the correct option is B.
